prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1–4, the depth map shows a horizontal clothing rack and hanging garments directly in front of the camera wearer within arm's reach at roughly 0.2–0.8 m (brightest on the left where garments are closest and fading to medium grey toward the right end of the rack at ~0.8–1.2 m), occluding the store background and windows above and behind the bar. In frame 3, the camera wearer's left hand enters from the bottom-center at ~0.2–0.3 m to touch a grey sweater, and in frame 4 the rack shifts downward and slightly farther (~0.4–1.0 m) as the camera wearer turns rightward and steps back. By frame 5, the camera wearer has turned right away from the rack (only a bright edge of clothing remains at ~0.3 m on the bottom-left) to face an open store interior where a woman with long dark hair stands in the center-right foreground at ~1.5–2.0 m looking toward the camera wearer, a hooded person in dark clothing stands ~0.5 m to her right (~2.0–2.5 m away) facing away toward a right-side glass doorway, and two further people near a mirror and wall rack on the left at ~3.0–4.0 m are mostly occluded. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground garment layers, the rack bar's front-to-back slant, and the distinct distance planes of the two foreground people versus the right wall and distant back wall (~4–6 m). However, the depth map is unreliable in the upper background of frames 1–3 where distant windows and a person peeking over the rack at upper-right in frame 3 are flattened into uniform black, and in frame 5 where the two distant people on the left merge into the dark background depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails to detect the clothing rack properly, instead misclassifying a plaid shirt on the far left (~1.0 m), the yellow size ring at top-left (~0.3 m), and a blue sweater sleeve at bottom-right (~0.3 m) in frame 1 as 'person' and 'banana', while leaving frame 2 and frame 4 completely blank despite the rack filling the foreground within arm's reach (~0.2–1.0 m). In frame 3, it merges nearly the entire foreground clothing rack and the camera wearer's reaching hand (~0.2–0.8 m) into one large pink 'person' mask, while separately segmenting the head and shoulders of a hat-wearing person standing ~2.0–2.5 m away behind the upper-right of the rack facing toward the camera wearer. In frame 5, after the camera wearer turns right, the map segments four 'person' instances from left to right: two partially occluded people standing ~0.5 m apart near a mirror on the left at ~3.0–4.0 m (cyan and purple masks, above a yellow mask on the foreground rack edge at ~0.3 m), the woman at bottom-center-right (~1.5–2.0 m, brown mask) whose body is cut off below the chest and who faces the camera wearer, and the person ~0.5 m to her right (~2.0–2.5 m, pink mask) facing away toward the right doorway. The segmentation map helps isolate the partially occluded person above the rack in frame 3 and clusters the four individuals in frame 5 against the cluttered retail background more distinctly than a quick glance at the RGB image. However, it is highly unreliable on hanging garments—hallucinating 'banana' and 'person' labels on clothes in frames 1 and 3 and missing the camera wearer's hand as a separate entity.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across frames 1–4, detecting neither the camera wearer's reaching left hand at ~0.2–0.3 m in frame 3 nor the partially occluded person peeking over the upper-right of the clothing rack at ~2.0–2.5 m, while the hanging garments within arm's reach (~0.2–1.0 m) occlude the rest of the room. Across frames 1–5, as the camera wearer releases the rack and turns rightward toward the open floor, the only skeleton keypoints appear in the lower-right of frame 5 on the woman standing at ~1.5–2.0 m in front of the camera wearer. Those yellow facial keypoints (eyes, nose, ears) and the nearly horizontal shoulder bar between her left and right shoulders show that her torso is angled slightly rightward toward the hooded person ~0.5 m to her right, while her head is turned left to face and look directly toward the camera wearer. This explicit geometric layout of her facial landmarks and shoulder axis confirms her head-versus-torso orientation more precisely than the low-resolution RGB crop alone. However, the pose map is largely unreliable for broader scene understanding because it misses her lower body (cut off by the bottom frame boundary), completely fails to detect the adjacent person ~0.5 m to her right (~2.0–2.5 m away, facing away) and the two distant people on the left (~3.0–4.0 m), and misses the camera wearer's hand in frame 3.
